items.title: Hong Kong Insurance Authority disciplines six intermediaries over AML and counter-terrorist-financing controls
items.grounded_note: Hong Kong’s Insurance Authority reported disciplinary action against six named insurance intermediaries for breaches of anti-money-laundering and counter-financing-of-terrorism controls. The action concerns Lam Nam, Lang Chit, Liang Shuxian, Ng Chi Wah, Yeung Chung Chak and Zhang Xindan. The authority’s enforcement listing establishes the AML/CFT basis and affected individuals but does not provide the detailed sanctions in the indexed entry.

items.title: Taiwan consults on security governance for financial institutions using agentic AI
items.grounded_note: Taiwan’s Financial Supervisory Commission issued a 30-day consultation document on the secure use of agentic AI across the financial sector, including insurers. It proposes managing each use case according to its purpose, accountable parties, accessible data and tools, permitted actions, output destinations, and arrangements for monitoring, shutdown, recovery and auditability. The framework would classify risk using data sensitivity, action impact and capability boundaries or propagation potential, while applying zero-trust concepts such as continuous verification, least privilege and traceability; the document is consultative and does not replace existing laws, outsourcing controls or internal-control requirements.

items.title: AXA Future Risks Report ranks AI and big data as experts’ leading emerging risk
items.grounded_note: AXA published the 13th edition of its Future Risks Report, produced with Ipsos, covering changing risk perceptions among experts and the public. Artificial intelligence and big-data risks ranked first among experts for the first time, moving ahead of climate change after ranking fourth in 2025. Among the public, AI rose from seventh to second place, while climate change remained the highest-ranked risk across generations.

items.title: MAS announces enhanced conduct safeguards for public prospecting activities
items.grounded_note: MAS announced that financial institutions will be expected to conduct public prospecting activities only in designated areas at commercial premises and appoint suitably qualified individuals to supervise representatives at those events. Representatives will be expected to disclose at the outset that they intend to market financial products or services and obtain the consumer's consent before continuing; street canvassing and door-to-door prospecting will remain prohibited. MAS plans to issue updated marketing and distribution conduct guidelines in 2027, after which financial institutions will receive a nine-month implementation period.

items.title: FWD to re-enter Hong Kong general insurance through 25% bolttech Insurance stake
items.grounded_note: FWD Group agreed to acquire a 25% stake in bolttech Insurance (Hong Kong) for a base consideration of US$20.72 million, marking FWD's planned return to Hong Kong's property-and-casualty insurance market. The target was formerly FWD General Insurance before FWD divested it to bolttech in 2020. The transaction represents a material portfolio expansion beyond FWD's principal life-insurance operations.

items.title: Malaysia's Budget 2027 measures support January 2027 rollout of MediAsas health coverage
items.grounded_note: BNM said the voluntary standardised MediAsas medical and health insurance/takaful plan will be rolled out to the public in January 2027. Premiums or contributions for coverage purchased for individuals and immediate family members will qualify for income-tax relief. The budget also allocates RM40 million for MediAsas vouchers for employees of SMEs with fewer than 75 employees, targeting workers who may have limited or no medical and health insurance or takaful coverage.

items.title: Mainland China issues Property Insurance Company Insurance Product Development Provisions
items.grounded_note: The National Financial Regulatory Administration issued revised provisions governing property insurance product development, comprising 41 articles across eight chapters and taking effect on November 1, 2026. The provisions make insurers legally responsible for their terms and rates, identify eight categories of products that may not be developed, prescribe requirements for primary and supplementary coverage, and require a product management committee led by the company’s principal officer. They also establish end-to-end governance from planning and internal review through regulatory filing, require assessment and remediation or withdrawal of products already on sale, and introduce annual reporting and internal accountability requirements.

items.title: Singapore life insurance body to review critical-illness definitions from 2027
items.grounded_note: MAS stated that the Life Insurance Association, Singapore will begin its next review of the Critical Illness Framework in 2027. The review will explore whether definitions for certain conditions can rely less on specified treatment procedures and more on the underlying disease and its severity. MAS noted that changes could affect coverage scope, claims experience and premiums, and that updated definitions would apply to newly sold products.

items.grounded_note: MAS issued Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management applying to all forms of AI used by financial institutions, including direct insurers, captive insurers and insurance brokers. items.title: MAS addresses proposal for seniors to access life insurance death benefits early
items.grounded_note: MAS said routine early access to life insurance death benefits would fundamentally alter the nature and pricing of policies that are underwritten on the basis that benefits are paid when the insured event occurs. It noted that some whole-life and endowment policies already permit access to accumulated cash value through withdrawals or policy loans, subject to policy terms, charges and a reduction in benefits ultimately payable. MAS said it would continue working with the insurance industry on product innovation for retirement, healthcare and long-term-care needs.

items.title: Taiwan proposes amendments governing insurers’ project, public-infrastructure and social-welfare investments
items.grounded_note: Taiwan’s Financial Supervisory Commission proposed amendments to rules governing insurers’ special-project, public-infrastructure and social-welfare investments. The draft removes the obsolete category of “emerging important strategic industries,” while allowing existing holdings in that category to remain and participate in capital increases under applicable requirements. It would also permit an insurer whose investment later falls under specified Insurance Act categories to participate in capital increases at its original ownership ratio where that ratio exceeds otherwise applicable statutory limits, including in connection with venture-capital investments that subsequently become publicly issued.

items.grounded_note: Taiwan’s Financial Supervisory Commission amended portions of the Regulations Governing the Preparation of Financial Reports by Insurance Enterprises. items.title: BNM assesses insurance transmission channels from Middle East conflict and energy disruption
items.grounded_note: BNM reported that Malaysian banks, insurers and takaful operators continued to maintain strong financial buffers, while the financial-stability effects of the Middle East conflict had remained manageable. It identified indirect insurance transmission channels including higher claims costs, valuation losses, pressure on earnings and capital generation, and reduced policy retention or demand as household and business cash flows weaken. BNM stated that these insurance demand effects had not materialised at the time of the assessment.

items.title: Taiwan introduces special-reserve rules for commercial earthquake and typhoon-flood insurance
items.grounded_note: Taiwan’s Financial Supervisory Commission issued immediately effective special-reserve rules for commercial earthquake and typhoon-flood insurance. Major-accident special reserves held for more than 30 years may be released as income; where retained actual claims after use of that reserve are below expected claims, insurers must place 75% of the difference into a fluctuation special reserve, using an expected loss ratio of at least 60%. Accumulated fluctuation reserves above 18 times annual retained earned premiums for commercial earthquake insurance or eight times for typhoon-flood insurance must be released as income.

items.title: AXA commits up to €470.8 million to neutralize Shareplan 2026 dilution
items.grounded_note: AXA entered into a share-repurchase agreement for a maximum of €470.8 million to offset the dilutive effect of its 2026 employee share offering. The shares will be repurchased for cancellation, with the purchase price based on the arithmetic average of daily volume-weighted average AXA share prices over 20 trading days beginning October 2, 2026. Transactions under the agreement are scheduled to end no later than October 29, 2026.

items.title: Fitbit connectivity with AIA Vitality Malaysia temporarily unavailable from 1 October 2026
items.grounded_note: AIA Malaysia said Fitbit connectivity with AIA Vitality became temporarily unavailable from 1 October 2026 because Google's existing Fitbit API was being replaced by the Google Health API, requiring a system migration. During the interruption, Fitbit workout and sleep data do not sync with AIA Vitality and members cannot earn AIA Vitality Points through Fitbit-based activity or sleep tracking. AIA directed members to alternatives including Apple Health, Samsung Health, Garmin, Polar, Huawei and Suunto while it works to restore Fitbit support; no restoration date was specified.
